headline: Why can't we see contamination?
caption: Why can't we see contamination? Microbes are far too small for the eye, so a surface can look spotless and still carry them. Argus detects microbial contamination invisible to the human eye.

headline: What is UV fluorescence?
caption: UV fluorescence: some materials absorb ultraviolet light and re-emit it as visible light. That glow can reveal what white light misses. It's the first layer in Argus.

headline: What is optical computer vision?
caption: Optical computer vision is software that reads images and turns what it sees into measurements. In Argus it works on what UV fluorescence reveals.

headline: Inference time, explained.
caption: Inference time is how long a model takes to produce a result from one input. Argus states 15 ms inference on its profile. Fast results are what make checking practical.

headline: Precision, explained.
caption: Precision: of everything a model flags, the share that is correct. Argus states 99.4% precision on its profile. In plain terms, about 994 of every 1,000 flags would be right.

headline: Looks clean vs is clean.
caption: Looks clean is what the eye can confirm. Is clean is what a measurement can confirm. They're not the same thing, and the gap is invisible by definition.

headline: Three layers, one pipeline.

headline: 15 ms. 99.4%.
